knowledge.text: Across the ten verified current pairs, every Parent and Candidate run succeeded. Outcome pattern: equal steps for P2/Q2 (4), P3/Q3 (7), P4/Q4 (4), and P9/Q9 (4); Candidate step reductions for P5/Q5 (18 vs 11), P6/Q6 (48 vs 5), P8/Q8 (15 vs 6), and P10/Q10 (14 vs 4); Candidate regressions for P1/Q1 (4 vs 5) and P7/Q7 (12 vs 29). Thus in this batch the joint edit was associated with both large search-phase gains and at least one large search-phase regression, not with task-completion failure.

Four current pairs showed large Candidate search-phase step reductions: P5→Q5 (18→11), P6→Q6 (48→5), P8→Q8 (15→6), and P10→Q10 (14→4), with both sides succeeding. In each, Candidate reached the target-bearing location earlier (dresser 1: P5:16/Q5:9; sidetable 1: P6:45/Q6:2 and P10:11/Q10:1; shelf 1: P8:12/Q8:3) and generally avoided or shortened the Parent's traversal of empty drawers or open-container cycles. Because Principles 2, 3, and 7 were changed together and Actor choices varied, these differences are a joint-intervention response, not isolated proof of one clause.

Counterexample limiting any uniform search-efficiency gain: on train:0006 (put some newspaper on sofa), P7 succeeded in 12 steps while Q7 succeeded in 29. After not finding the newspaper, Q7 repeatedly returned to coffeetable 1, sidetable 1, shelf 1, shelf 2, and the already-open drawer 1 across multiple cycles before finally reaching armchair 1 and taking newspaper 4; P7 visited the coffeetable, sidetable, and shelves, returned to coffeetable 1 once, then went directly to armchair 1 and succeeded. This shows the revised search/anti-cycle guidance did not prevent a long reintroduction cycle. The clause's reliance on the current observation and the last two observation/action pairs is consistent with such a longer cycle continuing undetected.

For already-open containers, on train:0005 (put a cellphone in shelf), P6 opened drawers 1-6 and then re-entered that same set of open drawers in repeated cycles without finding the cellphone, taking 48 steps and only succeeding after finally reaching sidetable 1. Q6 instead went desk 1→sidetable 1→took cellphone 1→shelf 1, never revisiting an open drawer, and succeeded in 5 steps. This is consistent with the revised guidance against re-opening or cycling through already-open containers being accompanied by reduced revisiting, but the run also reflects the post-acquisition direct-placement clause and Candidate prioritization, so clause isolation is not established.

When the required object or tool was found on the first visited surface and the search clause had little or no opportunity to change exploration, the edit preserved behavior and success: P2/Q2 (examine cd; both 4 steps), P3/Q3 (look at cd; both 7 steps), P4/Q4 (look at pillow; both 4 steps), and P9/Q9 (put soapbar in garbagecan; both 4 steps) had identical action sequences and both sides succeeded. This supports preserved capability for straightforward examine and pick-and-place tasks, though it is not evidence of improvement on those tasks.

Once the required object was acquired, the Candidate usually proceeded directly to the required next location for the task and succeeded. Examples include Q5 taking statue 1 then using desklamp 1, Q6 taking cellphone 1 then going to shelf 1 and placing it, Q8 taking pencil 3 then going to desk 1 and placing it, Q10 taking statue 1 then going to coffeetable 1 and placing it, and Q7 taking newspaper 4 then going to sofa 1 and placing it. This is consistent with the expanded post-acquisition clause, although the pairs also contain earlier search differences and do not isolate that clause.

Counterexample to uniform post-acquisition directness: on train:0000 (look at alarmclock under the desklamp), P1 succeeded in 4 steps and Q1 in 5. After taking alarmclock 2 from desk 1, Q1 made an extra search move to shelf 1 before going to dresser 1 and using desklamp 1, whereas P1 went directly from desk 1 to dresser 1 and used desklamp 1. Thus the expanded 'once acquired, stop searching and go directly to the required next location' guidance was not followed in this instance and did not eliminate a one-step search detour.
